pois.name: National Museum & Art Gallery
pois.wikipedia: en:National Museum and Art Gallery, Trinidad
pois.intro: The National Museum and Art Gallery is the national museum of Trinidad and Tobago, in Port of Spain on Trinidad island. It is located at the top of Frederick Street, opposite the Memorial Park, and just south of the Queen's Park Savannah.

pois.name: Royal Botanic Gardens
pois.intro: The Royal Botanic Gardens in Trinidad and Tobago is located in Port of Spain. The Gardens, which were established in 1818, are situated just north of the Queen's Park Savannah.

pois.name: Queen's Park Savannah
pois.intro: Queen's Park Savannah is a park in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago. Known locally as simply "the Savannah", it is Port of Spain's largest open space.

pois.name: Emperor Valley Zoo
pois.intro: The Emperor Valley Zoo is the only public zoo in Trinidad and Tobago. The 7.2-acre facility is located north of Queen's Park Savannah and west of the Royal Botanic Gardens, in Port of Spain.

pois.name: Archbishop's House
pois.description: The Archbishop's House, at 27 Maraval Road, is the official residence of the Archbishop of Port of Spain, which, as of 2016, is The Most Reverend Joseph Everard Harris, CSSP.
pois.intro: The Magnificent Seven is a group of seven mansions located west of the Queen's Park Savannah in northern Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago on Maraval Road in the St Clair neighborhood. They were built between 1902 and 1910 on land that was previously used as a government stock farm and are listed as heritage sites at the National Trust of Trinidad and Tobago.

pois.name: Queen's Royal College
pois.description: Queen's Royal College, a National Trust of Trinidad and Tobago listed building, was built on the corner of St Clair Avenue & Maraval Road beginning 11 November 1902, when the foundation stone was placed by the acting governor of the day, Courtney Knollys.
pois.intro: Queen's Royal College, referred to for short as QRC, or "The College" by alumni, is a secondary school in Trinidad and Tobago. Originally a boarding school and grammar school, the secular college is selective and noted for its German Renaissance architecture, academic performance and alumni representation in sports, politics and science in Trinidad and Tobago and globally.

pois.name: Knowsley Building
pois.address: 1 Queen's Park West, Port of Spain
pois.description: Knowsley occupies a city block facing Port of Spain’s Queen’s Park Savannah and bounded by Chancery Lane, Dundonald Street and Albion Lane.  The building was designed and built in 1904 by Taylor and Gillies for William Gordon as his residence.

pois.name: Hayes Court
pois.description: Hayes Court, at 21 Maraval Road, was built as a residence for the Anglican Bishop to Trinidad. An anonymous gift was made in 1908 by two men to pay for the construction of the building, which was built in a French Colonial architectural style.

pois.name: Mille Fleurs
pois.description: Mille Fleurs at 23 Maraval Road was built and named by the wife of Dr Enrique Prada (1867 Venezuela–1944 Trinidad) in 1904.

pois.name: Whitehall
pois.description: White Hall, on 29 Maraval Road, is the largest residence on its road. Originally called Rosenweg, it was built by Joseph Leon Agostini, a cocoa planter, based upon his design plans.

pois.intro: Memorial Park is an urban park in upper Downtown, Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago. Memorial Park is a public city park in commemoration of the Trinidadian veterans that served in World War I and World War II. It is one of the most visited urban parks in the city.
